restrictions: The system is Windows 2000 build 2195 RTM with NO service pack, not Windows 2000 SP4: this verdict says nothing about SP4 (the plan, research R6, spike S1 and task T066 name SP4). The system DLLs read here are the RTM ones (kernel32.dll 5.0.2191.1, user32.dll 5.0.2180.1, msvcrt.dll 6.1.8637.0, dated 1999-12-07); SP4 replaces them with later builds, so the export tables confirmed here (tools/win2000_imports.json, confidence verified-on-vm) are those of RTM. Exports only grow from RTM to SP4, which makes a missing function on SP4 unlikely, but that was not checked.

Only one machine and one configuration, and an emulated one: VirtualBox 7.2.22 on a Windows 11 host, 1 vCPU, 168 MB RAM, VirtualBox Graphics Adapter 800x600x32 at 96 DPI, English (US) system with a French AZERTY keyboard layout for the user. No real hardware (physical chipset, display driver, input devices), no other Windows 2000 installation, language, edition (Server, Advanced Server) or hardware. Timings and memory are those of this VM: display_ms 3 to 13 ms and a constant peak_rss_kb of 1084 over the 20 '--probe' runs are not figures for real hardware.

Typing was exercised through the virtual keyboard of VirtualBox, not by a person: 'VBoxManage controlvm keyboardputstring Marie' assumes a US layout and the guest layout is French AZERTY, so it typed '?qrie' (the window then read 'Bonjour ?qrie', window-3-keyboardputstring.png); 'Marie' was then typed with the scancodes of the physical keys that give M, a, r, i, e on AZERTY (Home, Shift+End to select the prefilled text first) and the window read 'Marie' / 'Bonjour Marie' (window-4-typed-marie.png). The update delay of the greeting (User Story 1: within 1 second) was NOT measured: a screenshot is taken 1.5 s after the keys and shows the label already updated. No input method (IME), no clipboard paste, no typing of accented or non-Latin characters with the keyboard (those were only given through --probe-input), no mouse click on the field or on the close button (the window was closed with Alt+F4, scancodes).

The 1,000-character limit of the EDIT control was not tried with the keyboard on this system (no 1,100 keystrokes); text given by --probe-input bypasses that limit and is cut by the application itself (probe.cpp): the three vectors longer than 1,000 UTF-16 units (limit_4096_ascii, limit_4096_two_byte_chars, and in the extra battery 1,100 and 1,500 characters and 998 'a' + an emoji) were cut at 1,000 units without splitting a surrogate pair, as expected.

Glyph drawing: the probe checks the text of the greeting, and tools/run_vectors.py checks it character for character (15 of 15 reference vectors and 25 of 25 extra hard vectors), but this system's fonts do not draw everything. In a probe-mode window with 'Zoé Hélène çà 日本語 שלום 😀' (window-6-nonascii-probe.png, viewed by the author of the trial) the accented Latin letters are drawn correctly, the three CJK characters appear as three narrow missing-glyph boxes, the emoji (two UTF-16 units) as two such boxes, and the Hebrew letters are drawn (their order on screen was not checked). Nothing is garbled in the string itself.

No high contrast scheme, no DPI above 96 and no dark theme were tried: HKCU HighContrast Flags 126 (off), Win32_DisplayConfiguration.LogPixels 96, the AppsUseLightTheme value does not exist on this system. The Legacy UI took the skipped-feature path for two optional features, 'dpi-awareness' (user32.dll of this system does not export SetProcessDPIAware) and 'dark-mode' (no AppsUseLightTheme value), and displayed normally; 'high-contrast-query' (SystemParametersInfoW is exported) and 'peak-memory' (psapi.dll and GetProcessMemoryInfo exist) were available. The 4.5:1 contrast ratio of ui-contract item 2 was not measured (system colours are used).

The backend self-test could not be run on this system (spike S1 / T066 asks for it): loomora_selftest cross-built with cmake/toolchains/mingw-w64-win2000-i686.cmake imports KERNEL32!GetThreadId and four Vista-only condition-variable functions (InitializeConditionVariable, SleepConditionVariableCS, WakeConditionVariable, WakeAllConditionVariable) through libgcc.a(gthr-win32-cond.o) and libgcc.a(gthr-win32.o), pulled in by its use of <iostream>; the loader of this system refuses it (errorlevel 128, nothing printed), with the GetThreadId shim of ADR 0002 linked as well (selftest-run.json, same as the control program vista.exe). The Legacy UI executable, which links the same backend library libloomora.a but no iostream, does not have these imports and runs; so the backend is exercised here only through the UI (probe, 15 + 25 vectors).

The verdict covers the x86 executable out/windows-legacy/x86/loomora.exe (sha256 16e7859665c330a601f2d2afe15c8e955f64747c3533886a96de3a08f237494e) as built at commit d7f84de with MinGW-w64 GCC 13; it was started with CreateProcessW from a guest helper (tools/guest/runw.c, built with the same compiler), not by a double click in Explorer or from a command prompt typed by a person, and the guest processes were counted with WMI (Windows 2000 has no tasklist or taskkill). The helper's own run of the window without --probe used --nowait.

No procedure document exists yet for this trial (validation/procedures/windows.md is task T109), so the verdict carries no 'reproduction' path; the commands are in the 'notes' field and the driver script is part of the evidence.

The platform record windows-2000-x86 has no deliverable record of its own: the build writes validation/deliverables/windows-x86-legacy.json under the platform id windows-x86 (same executable), which tools/validate_records.py reports as a warning, as for the Windows 11 verdict.
disabled_features: dpi-awareness (user32.dll of this system does not export SetProcessDPIAware; no DPI virtualisation exists before Windows Vista, the window is drawn at 96 DPI)
dark-mode (no AppsUseLightTheme value on this system: no dark theme setting for applications; system colours used)

The 10 probe lines of '--probe --probe-input Marie': display_ms 4 to 13 (median 9), peak_rss_kb 1084 in all 10.

Source of the control program memtest.exe: GetProcessMemoryInfo before and after touching 8 MB allocated with VirtualAlloc.

Output of memtest.exe on this system: peakWS 596 KB at start, 8840 KB after touching 8 MB, kept after the free, so GetProcessMemoryInfo reports plausible and responsive numbers on Windows 2000; a bare process counts about 600 KB.

Independent measure of the peak_rss_kb of a running loomora.exe: WMI Win32_Process polled every 300 ms from another process gives WorkingSetSize = PeakWorkingSetSize = 1,093,632 bytes (1068 KB) while the probe line of that same run says peak_rss_kb 1084: the figure is plausible (the working set of a Windows 2000 process only counts the pages it touched).
The read-only VBScript that polled the process memory through WMI.

notes: Windows 2000 trial of the Windows Legacy UI (x86 executable) in a VirtualBox VM, 2026-11-12, on the platform described in validation/platforms/windows-2000-x86.json (Windows 2000 build 2195, NO service pack). It covers the Windows 2000 part of T088, the Windows 2000 evidence of T094 and spike S1 / T066 for what it names; it is the Legacy floor CANDIDATE for the Windows family only for what was actually tested on this VM (FR-005: the oldest platform on which the greeting really displays), and says nothing about SP4. What works on this system: the executable loads (112 of 112 imports exported), shows the window with the end-of-life banner, 'Bonjour Coucou', updates to 'Bonjour Marie' when typed with the virtual keyboard, takes the skipped-feature path for DPI awareness and dark mode, writes a valid probe line (20 of 20 runs, 15 + 25 of 40 vectors), exits cleanly after 2 s and with Alt+F4, and leaves no process. What does not: the backend self-test loomora_selftest cannot be loaded (Vista-only imports from libgcc's condition-variable code, see the restrictions), and the guest's fonts do not draw CJK or emoji. Commands (repository root, Windows 11 host, VM already running and logged on; LOOMORA_VM_NAME, LOOMORA_VM_USER and LOOMORA_VM_PASSWORD only needed if they differ from 'Windows 2000', 'name' and empty): 'wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 --cd <repo> -- python3 tools/build.py windows legacy', 'python tools/trials/windows-2000-x86/trial-driver.py' (facts, exports, runs, memory, gui, glyphs, selftest; the selftest step needs 'sh tools/guest/build_selftest.sh' and 'sh tools/trials/windows-2000-x86/loader-control.sh' in WSL first), 'python tools/run_vectors.py windows-2000-x86 legacy --evidence-dir validation/evidence/first-trial/windows-2000-x86/', and 'python tools/check_imports.py --verify-dlls <folder of the copied system DLLs>'. How the guest is driven: the old Guest Additions (6.1.18) do not pass command-line arguments to a guest program, and Windows Script Host 5.1 (WshShell.Run) converts the command line to the ANSI code page ('?' for every other character, measured) and expands %VARIABLES%, so each run copies cmdline.txt (UTF-16LE) and runs run.bat, which starts tools/guest/runw.c (kernel32 only, 5.5 KB); it reads the command line, calls CreateProcessW, waits and prints the exit status, the probe line and the leftover process count back through VBoxManage guestcontrol run. The guest folder created for the trial (C:\Documents and Settings\name\loomora-vectors) was deleted afterwards; the VM was left running as found, no snapshot was restored. The text files of this evidence folder keep their LF line endings (validation/evidence/.gitattributes marks them -text) because the verdict holds their sha256.
